title: Wrap a failed fetch, keeping the IOException as the cause

blocks.text: Inside a `catch` block, `throw` can raise a new exception that wraps the caught one as its cause (exception chaining). `ReportException`, a checked exception, is given. Write `ReportReader`:

items: `String read(String name) throws ReportException` returns `source.fetch(name)`. When `fetch` throws an `IOException`, `read` throws `ReportException` with the message `Could not read report <name>`.

blocks.text: Someone reading the log later still needs to see why the fetch failed, and a bug in the source (an unchecked exception) is not a failed read.

cases.says: A report the source can fetch is returned as it is.
A failed fetch is thrown as ReportException("Could not read report <name>").
The IOException is passed as the cause, so its message survives as the root cause and "Caused by:" appears in the trace.
Only the IOException is translated; an unchecked exception from the source propagates as the same object.

concepts: A checked exception thrown with throw must be caught or declared with throws.
Throw the most specific type, so callers can catch it selectively.
When a catch block throws a new exception, the caught one is passed as its cause.
